facts.statement: The genus Judinornis was described by Nessov and Borkin in 1983.
The only known species of this genus is Judinornis nogontsavensis.
Judinornis was a prehistoric flightless bird that lived during the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Judinornis is a genus of prehistoric flightless birds from the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Judinornis have been found in the Nemegt Formation of southern Mongolia.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in Nemegt Formation rocks of southern Mongolia

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives, Judinornis apparently inhabited estuaries and rivers flowing from the mountains of East Asia toward the Turgai Sea and the former Shigatze Ocean.
facts.quote: The Nemegt Formation does not seem to contain marine sediments. Consequently, and unlike its relatives, this was apparently a bird of estuaries and rivers running from the mountains thrown up by the Cimmerian orogeny through the arid lands of continental East Asia towards the Turgai Sea and the former Shigatze Ocean.

facts.statement: Judinornis was a member of the Hesperornithes, a group of flightless, toothed seabirds from the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Judinornis was a member of the Hesperornithes, flightless toothed seabirds of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Judinornis belongs to the family Baptornithidae.
Judinornis lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Judinornis likely lived approximately 70 million years ago during the early Maastrichtian stage.
rejected.quote: Judinornis probably lived some 70 million years ago during the early Maastrichtian.
